sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 15-02-2021 at about 1.30 pm., the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-40-EE-3432 in front of Chikkajala Law & Order Station, B.B.Road, NH-7,
Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Car, bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MP-5051 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle.

entities.text: Chikkajala Law & Order Station, B.B.Road, NH-7,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to impact petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately petitioner was shifted to Ashwini Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took first aid treatment and then shifted to Manasa Hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and diagnosed he sustained grievous injuries as per wound certificate.
The petitioner has spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards treatment, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.
The petitioner was discharged with an advise to take follow-up treatment.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was self employed and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has lost entire earning capacity and future earning capacity.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Chikkajala Police have registered a Criminal Case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.37/2021 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279 & 337 of IPC.
After investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents being Insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.1790/2021 compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.
The respondent No.2 remained absent and was placed exparte.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is as under:
This respondent denies petition averments specifically and categorically.
This respondent has denied manner of accident and averments mentioned in the petition.
It has contended that issuance of insurance policy in respect of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MP-5051 and the liability if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
As per Sec.134(c) of MV Act, the 2 nd respondent has not complied the conditions of the policy, hence this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This respondent has specifically denies the occurrence, mode of accident and also involvement of vehicle of offending vehicle.

The driver (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.1790/2021 of offending vehicle was not holding effective and valid driving license as on the date of accident and policy condition is violated and, hence this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation.

It has specifically denied the place,
time and manner of accident.
It has also denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The alleged accident is caused on the sole negligence of petitioner himself.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 15-02-2021 at about 1.30 pm., in front of Chikkajala Law & Order Station, B.B.Road, NH-7, Bangalore due to rash and negligent act of driving of Ford Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MP-5051 by its driver as alleged in the petition?

entities.text: Chikkajala Law & Order Station, B.B.Road, NH-7,
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation?
from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
On the other hand, 1st respondent has examined its Legal Manager as RW1 and no documents were got marked.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.
7.

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
-:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:- It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 15.02.2021 at about 1:30 Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109163706/
3 pm., the petitioner was met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MP-5051 while he was traveling on the motor cycle and due to impact he sustained injuries.

entities.text: Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also relied documents at Ex.P1 to P11.

The Ex.P1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P3 is the Sketch , Ex.P4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 & 6 are the IMV Report, Ex.P7 is the charge Sheet, Ex.P8 is the wound certificate, Ex.P9 is the discharge summary, Ex.P10 is the driving license and Ex.P11 is the medical bills.

10. On perusal of these documents, it shows that one Rajendra Prasad.K.N has lodged First Information statement before Chikkajala Traffic Police Station, alleging that on 15.12.2021 at about 1.30 pm., his friend Madhukumar.
A herein petitioner met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing No.KA-02-MP- 5051 while his friend was traveling on the motor cycle and sustained injuries.
On the basis of this first Information statement the Chikkajala Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.37/2021 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

Thereafter, the Investigating Officer (SCCH-9)
8 MVC.No.1790/2021 had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable Under Sec.279 & 337 of IPC.
11.
The respondent No.1 contended that the driver of offending Car was not responsible for the cause of alleged accident.
The accident was caused only due to sole negligence of petitioner himself.
Therefore the respondent No.1 is not liable to pay the compensation.
I have perused the materials available on record.
The charge sheet filed by investigating officer leveled charges of rash and negligent act of the driver of offending Car.
Though respondent No.1 examined its official as RW1 but this witness is not eye witness to the accident.
Only on self swearing statement of this RW1 it cannot be held that no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the petitioner, who was the eye witness to the accident clearly stated that accident in question was caused by the driver of offending vehicle.
The PW1 was elaborately cross- examined by the respondent no.1 but nothing was elicited to disbelieve evidence of PW1.
(SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.1790/2021 12. Further the Ex.P5 & 6 are the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports also discloses that the offending vehicle as well as petitioner's vehicle were damaged.
It is material to note that there is no explanation by the Owner of offending vehicle regarding damages caused to the vehicle.
13. It is settled principles of law that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to fastened the negligence on the driver of offending vehicle.
It is the petitioner who has come to the court seeking relief must prove the negligence independently in a claim petition.

As stated above the Ex.P5 & 6 Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109163706/
4 IMV Reports clearly shows that the negligence on the part of the rider of offending motor cycle as such damages were caused.

entities.text: Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Ex.P3 hand sketch also goes to show that the place of accident is a straight road, there is no zig-zag road.
The Ex.p3 also goes to show that the driver of offending vehicle has taken his vehicle extremely towards left side of the road and caused the accident.

Further, Ex.P3 shows that there is a sufficient width on the road inspite of that, the driver of offending (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.1790/2021 vehicle has taken his vehicle to the extreme left side of the road and caused the accident while going towards service road.
14. The learned counsel for the 1 st respondent tried to elicited in the cross-examination of PW1 that there is four days delay in lodging the complaint.
Since the injured has sustained severe injuries and as such we cannot expect to lodge the complaint by the injured soon after the accident.

Normally,
injured person will give preference to take treatment rather than compliance of legal requirements.
Same has been done by the petitioner in this case.
Therefore, the question of delay losses its significance.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in a reported decision (2011) 4 SCC 693 (Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana,) wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.

Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.1790/2021 kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.

Delay in lodging the FIR thus,
cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

15. At the time of arguments, the learned counsel (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.1790/2021 for respondent No.1 drawn the attention of the Court with regard to wound certificate Ex.P8 and mentioning history as self fall from bike.
The learned counsel vehemently argued and submitted that it is a self fall case not RTA case hence case of the petitioner cannot be believable.
The car has been implicated to get the compensation.
In this regard, he has relied judgment of our own Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in a case between National Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s Rajanna S/o.Narayanappa.

entities.text: National Insurance Co., Ltd., V/s Rajanna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in Ex.P8 the Doctor has mentioned history as - Self Fall from Bike.
But the respondent No.1 has not taken any steps to examine the doctor, who has written the said history.
Further, in discharge summary history mentioned as RTA.
When 1st respondent took specific contention about self fall case, it is his burden to prove the same.
The respondent No.1 has not discharged his burden by adducing the cogent evidence.
Therefore, only on mentioning of history as self fall in wound certificate it cannot be said that the case of the petitioner cannot be believable one.
So far as, the judgment is concerned the facts and circumstances of the (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.1790/2021 said case are different.
Hence not helpful to the 1 st respondent.

Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109163706/
5 16.

entities.text: Madhu Kumar A vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That apart in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.
This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).

Under such circumstances, in the instant case, there are sufficient materials to hold that the driver of offending Car has caused the accident with rash and negligent manner and as a result petitioner sustained injuries.
Further there is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1 with regard to cause of accident.
Under such circumstances, it is held that the petitioner has proved the issue No.1
With this observations and discussion, I answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:
This petition is filed for seeking (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.1790/2021 compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the RTA.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
As per Ex.P5/wound certificate the petitioner has contended that he sustained - Multiple abrasions over face, upper and lower limb and right upper bone.
18. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and also not produced any disability certificate to show that he is having physical disability.

Therefore, in view of non production of disability certificate and non examining of doctor regarding disability, it cannot be considered as the petitioner is having physical disability due to the accidental injuries.
The petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P11 amounting to Rs.51,960/-.

On perusal of Ex.P9/discharge summary of Manasa Hospital Bangalore, it discloses that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 15.02.2022 to 22.02.2022.
19.
As stated above there is no physical disability (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.1790/2021 caused to the petitioner due to the accidental injuries.
Therefore, there is no question of awarding compensation for loss of future earnings.

Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained, treatment taken,
medical bills produced it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation.

Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
20.
Regarding Liability:
The respondent no.1 took a contention that it had issued insurance policy in favour of 2nd respondent in respect to offending vehicle but liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It shows that there is no dispute about issuance of insurance policy, which was valid at the time of accident.
Further, materials shows that there is no violation of policy condition by the 2nd respondent.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However,
the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.1790/2021 compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
21. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.1,00,000/- (One Lakh Only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.1790/2021 and verification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
